title: Exact pairs and failure of meets in the Turing degrees
summary: Construct a pair whose common Turing lower bounds are exactly those below a given increasing sequence, and deduce that some degree pairs have no greatest lower bound.
abstract: Two Turing degrees can share information without there being a strongest problem recoverable from both. We construct a pair whose common lower bounds are exactly the problems reducible to one term of a prescribed increasing sequence. Each side stores that sequence in columns, with only finitely many errors in each column. When two programs agree on a total output, a search using finitely many protected columns recovers the output. Applied to the successive halting problems, the construction gives two degrees with no greatest common lower bound. The proof includes the finite-error corrections and total-oracle search needed to make the column argument precise.
